svg.title: Task workflow: new ticket to verified release
svg.desc: Free-form workflow map with physical runtime boundaries, one coding-session CI loop, independent semantic test-strength review, Jev decisions through WFJev, human gates and QA returns. Grok bot fleet: WFTasks, WFJev, WFReview, WFCoder, WFRelease.
svg.text: Jev decides readiness. Workers implement. Independent reviewers challenge both the code and its tests.
SUPERSET HANDOFF: ticket ID + operational notes + execution instructions only. Never the title or copied ticket content.
GROK BOT APP · WFTasks + WFJev + WFCoder
A new tracker issue ID is available.
Read description, existing ticket AC, relations and
Tracker integration; ticket text and image inspection.
Intent and evidence understood. Missing source
Ticket description and explicit AC are loaded.
AC present, clear, testable, consistent; enough
Jev checks + source facts. Never infer or create AC.
All AC gates pass; owner, model, capacity and
Task approved for work; capacity reserved.
Start or resume one Superset session.
Ticket ID, operational notes and execution
Session confirmed. Task name uses the issue ID; no
Update the ticket and return it to WFTasks (01). WFTasks
rereads the current ticket, then asks Jev (02). Never guess
Dependencies / capacity pending? Wait for the event; no
Models: Grok · Claude Opus · Claude Fable · ChatGPT Sol · ChatGPT Astra
Coding agent owns planning, implementation and the CI correction loop.
Static, unit, integration, mutation, browser and
CI access / infrastructure blocked → pause. A lost session needs controller recovery.
Current PR and acceptance evidence are available.
Choose a bounded review or deeper behavior
Assess business logic, integrations, risk and QA
External review route selected; required human
Bounded change; configured review coverage is sufficient.
Externally started; never the implementation session or its child reviewer.
Current ticket AC, Verification Plan, candidate head and actual test results.
Check AC ↔ scenarios ↔ tests ↔ code. Verify that each test would detect a meaningful violation of
Independent counterexample search; test-strength analysis; targeted mutation where useful.
Per-AC VERIFIED, FAILED or UNVERIFIED, with test-strength evidence, counterexamples and explicit
Would these tests fail if the implementation violated the actual AC?
expect(component).toBeDefined() does not prove container-based layout. Try a container → viewport substitution:
would the test fail? Record which meaningful AC violation each test detects.
Reviewed build is available in develop.
Validate the accepted feature or bug fix.
Acceptance scenarios, regression checks and screenshots.
Explicit QA pass tied to this build and the requirements.
Resolve the named decision. Return the update to WFTasks
(05), which refreshes context before review resumes.
Session checks challenge code changes. 06B challenges
violations of the real acceptance criteria.
WFRelease holds the candidate and refreshes evidence.
QA moved the ticket to Ready for Staging on the reviewed head;
the stand comment matches that head.
Refresh head, CI, review, approvals and release window; hold the
candidate while a blocker or human decision is pending.
WFRelease tracks release timing, approvals and updated
source evidence; no dispatch while waiting.
Evidence refreshed → 09. Wait resolved or human update →
WFRelease refreshed evidence in 08; required checks pass.
Jev completion: automatic staging merge now, or wait for a
Fresh gates, branch rules, release window and the merge
grant; Jev flags scope, manual checks, coordination.
All gates and the merge grant → 10. Otherwise → 08 with
Merge and deployment actions are authorized.

Merge once; reconcile existing actions; deploy and
Release succeeds; deployed version and health are
Resolve or approve the named release action. Return the update to
WFRelease (08); it reloads current evidence before step 09.
Staging release succeeded; exact build is known.
Explicit QA pass on the staged artifact; blocking
QA Staging passed on the exact staged artifact.
Refresh artifact, CI, QA Staging, incidents, freeze,
batch, permissions; hold while a decision is pending.
WFRelease tracks release timing, approvals and evidence.
Evidence refreshed → 13. Human update → refresh and
Production gates and the release grant pass.
Merge to the production branch; CI deploys it.
Deployment, actual version and health / smoke checks.
Verified delivery → ticket moved to Done. Failure →
HUMAN · production release owner, when required
Return the release decision to WFRelease (12). It refreshes evidence before
WFJev re-evaluates. A model score never grants deployment permission.
Deployment failed or outcome unknown? Hold the stage, reconcile or recover, then
recheck. Never advance on dispatch alone.
QA RETURN · validate the report before another coding attempt
GROK BOT APP · WFTasks + WFJev; WFCoder takes validated rework
New QA feedback is retrieved from the tracker.
Check completeness, tested build, failure relation and ownership.
Expected / actual result, steps, environment and image evidence.
Confirmed failure or regression on the correct build. Skip videos; video reports
Failure confirmed; owner and worker eligibility checked.
Start the next bounded implementation attempt.
Ticket ID + operational notes only; worker reads QA itself.
New fix evidence, then fresh independent behavior review.
Ask for details or a decision
Report incomplete, tested build stale, or new scope / owner needed.
Resolve only the missing evidence or named decision.
Screenshots + written repro; correct-build retest; scope clarification.
Updated report → step 15. Do not launch coding while the report is insufficient.
WFRelease refreshed evidence in 12; QA Staging passed
Stricter Jev completion for production release: no
risk class, incident, freeze or batch blocker.
Fresh gates, rollout and recovery plan, batch,
freeze, approvals and the production grant.
All gates and the grant → 14. Otherwise → human
release owner; back through WFRelease 12, then 13.
09 → 10 · automatic merge authorized; all current gates pass
Sources: WFTasks reads the tracker; workers read the tracker + linked designs • image attachments only • stop on missing access • no self-review • only WFJev invokes Jev.
WHAT: ticket AC / human owner • HOW: Verification Plan / planner • PROOF: independent review of code AND test strength.
Current ticket AC and repository instructions are loaded by the worker.
Plan HOW to prove existing AC; implement code and meaningful tests.
Run checks, follow CI and fix code/test failures within this same session.
Never create, expand or improve AC. Independent review stays external.
Repository-configured agent workflow, local checks and CI.
Grok status hooks report activity, blockers and completion candidates.
Completion candidate → controller reconciles session, PR head and evidence → 05.
A Stop / SessionEnd hook alone does not prove task completion.
Activity → keep running. Blocked / stuck → inspect or wait.
Stop / end → reconcile once before step 05.
Tool and child events do not complete the parent task.
